sections.label: Two anti-money laundering Bills
sections.summary: The House will debate the Corporate Service Providers Bill and the Companies and Limited Liability Partnerships (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill to strengthen Singapore's anti-money laundering regime.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Today, the House will be debating two Bills which are intended to strengthen Singapore's anti-money laundering regime.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: First, the Corporate Service Providers Bill (CSP Bill), to enhance our regulatory regime for corporate service providers; and second, the Companies and Limited Liability Partnerships (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill, which will complement the CSP Bill by enhancing the transparency of companies and limited liability partnerships (LLPs).

sections.label: Corporate service provider filings
sections.summary: These transactions involve statutory filing of documents for corporate secretarial services, with nearly 3,000 ACRA-regulated CSPs accounting for 70% of ACRA's filing transactions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: These transactions involve the statutory filing of documents in the course of providing corporate secretarial services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: There are nearly 3,000 CSPs regulated by ACRA today, and filings done by these CSPs account for 70% of ACRA's filing transactions.

sections.label: Higher sanctions for CSP non-compliance
sections.summary: Sanctions for CSP non-compliance with obligations to detect and prevent money laundering will increase from a $25,000 financial penalty to a $100,000 fine.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We will tighten our regulations for breaches of obligations to combat financial crime.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We will increase the sanctions for non-compliance by CSPs of their obligations to detect and prevent money laundering, from the existing financial penalty of $25,000 to a fine of $100,000.

sections.label: Nominee director business requirement
sections.summary: Individuals may act as nominee directors by way of business only if arranged by a CSP, unless they are sole proprietors of a registered CSP, with breaches fined up to $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: First, we will require that individuals can only act as a nominee director by way of business if the nominee directorship was arranged by a CSP, unless the individual himself is the sole proprietor of a registered CSP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This could include a scenario in which, for example, an individual receives a fee for providing such services to his clients.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Those found guilty of breaching this requirement can face a fine of up to $10,000.

sections.label: CSP breach fine
sections.summary: CSPs found guilty of breaching this requirement can face a fine of up to $100,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: CSPs who are found guilty of breaching this requirement, can face a fine of up to $100,000.

sections.label: Higher penalties for register offences
sections.summary: Maximum penalties for companies and LLPs committing offences relating to their registers will be raised from $5,000 to $25,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: First, we will raise the maximum penalties for companies and LLPs that commit offences relating to their registers, from $5,000 to $25,000.

sections.label: Registration of corporate service providers
sections.summary: Requires entities carrying on corporate service business in Singapore to register as registered CSPs, replacing the term RFA with CSP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: First, to require companies and other entities that carry on a business in Singapore of providing any corporate service to be registered as a registered CSP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This will cover companies that provide registration of shell companies in overseas jurisdictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: It also means that the term RFA will no longer be used and will be replaced by the term "corporate service provider" or CSP.

sections.label: Criminal liability and fines for CSPs
sections.summary: The Act imposes criminal liability on registered CSPs and their senior management, with fines up to $100,000 per breach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Act imposes criminal liability on registered CSPs and their senior management with hefty fines of up to $100,000 for each breach.

sections.label: ACRA cancelled RFA and RQI registrations
sections.summary: In the last three years, ACRA cancelled the registrations of 17 RFAs and 17 RQIs, based on a Straits Times report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: As it is, within the last three years, ACRA has cancelled the registrations of 17 RFAs and 17 RQIs, based on The Straits Times report today.

sections.label: Banks as better gatekeepers
sections.summary: The speaker submits banks and financial institutions are better gatekeepers against money laundering, so huge penalties on CSPs are unnecessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Here, I would submit that banks and financial institutions are in a better position to be the gatekeeper against money laundering, rather than CSPs, because the funds flow through the banks and financial institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Thus, there should not be a need to impose such huge penalties on CSPs who may have been careless or negligently failed to carry out their CDD.

sections.label: Guidelines for fit and proper nominee directors
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister whether clear guidelines will be issued for CSPs to determine who is a fit and proper nominee director.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Next, may I ask the Minister whether there would be clear guidelines issued to enable CSPs to determine who is considered a fit and proper person to be a nominee director.

sections.label: Guidelines for AML and CFT compliance
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to provide clear guidelines to CSPs on AML and CFT criteria, warning of losing competitive edge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Personally, I, too, have been rejected by banks when I tried to open a simple deposit account with the bank simply because I am a PEP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Thus, I urge the Government to provide clear guidelines to CSPs so that they know what are the criteria they have to assess in complying with AML and CFT requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: If a foreigner has to wait for months to start a business or to open a bank account in Singapore, the risk is that we will lose our competitive edge as a business-friendly country.

sections.label: Singaporean director 980 companies
sections.summary: A Singaporean who directed 980 companies was sentenced under the Companies Act, with over US$5 million laundered through some companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In December last year, it was reported that a Singaporean was helping his clients from China set up companies in Singapore and became a director of a whopping 980 companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: He was subsequently sentenced to multiple charges of failing to exercise his duties as a director and other related charges under the Companies Act, with more than US$5 million being laundered through some of the companies under him.

sections.label: Clause 16 nominee director training
sections.summary: Clause 16 requires a registered CSP to be satisfied a nominee director is fit and proper, but a training proposal was not proceeded with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While the introduction of clause 16 of the Bill meant that a registered CSP must not arrange for a person to act as a nominee director of a company unless he is satisfied that the person is fit and proper, the proposal to require CSPs to ensure appointed nominee directors satisfy prescribed training requirements if they hold more than a legally prescribed number of nominee directorships by way of business was, ultimately, not proceeded with.

sections.label: Minister's estimate nominee directors covered
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister to estimate how many nominee directors the new proposal would have covered, noting 99% of directors hold fewer than 10 directorships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: What is the Minister's estimate of the number of nominee directors who would have been covered under this new proposal, especially when 99% of directors hold fewer than 10 directorships and that many nominee directors are likely to be qualified persons themselves?

sections.label: Registered Filing Agents and Qualified Individuals
sections.summary: There were close to 2,800 Registered Filing Agents and 3,500 Registered Qualified Individuals in Singapore at the end of 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Next, I recognise that there are close to 2,800 Registered Filing Agents (RFAs) and 3,500 Registered Qualified Individuals in Singapore as at the end of 2023.

sections.label: CSP key appointment holders training
sections.summary: Under section 9(1)(e), CSP registration or renewal is refused if key appointment holders did not complete a prescribed course or training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In addition, under section 9(1)(e) of the Bill, registration or renewal of a CSP will be refused if any of the key appointment holders did not successfully complete a prescribed course or training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In addition, as the definition of key appointment holders is sufficiently broad such that "any person who is principally responsible for the management and conduct of X's business activities in providing corporate services" would be considered a key appointment holder, there could be a large number of company employees that would have managerial responsibilities, albeit being a junior member of the company, and the level of scrutiny and standards required of a qualified individual (QI) supervising the CSP should be well higher than that of a junior assistant manager.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To what extent do the current provisions in the Bill mean that duplicate registration is required and, hence, duplicate monitoring of the clients for money laundering risks?

sections.label: Money laundering events surged Singapore
sections.summary: Moody's data show money laundering events in Singapore surged 79% year-on-year, after a S$3 billion money laundering incident last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We have a good reputation for our robust regulatory framework and our commitment to uphold high standards of integrity in the financial sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: However, recent data from Moody's show that money laundering events in Singapore surged by 79% year-on-year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This is not surprising, considering that Singapore faced and tackled decisively the largest money laundering incident last year involving S$3 billion of illicit funds.

sections.label: Cooling-off period for cancelled CSPs
sections.summary: Section 9(2)(f) requires the Registrar to decline re-registration for CSPs whose previous registration was cancelled within two years for non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Notably, section 9(2)(f) stipulates that the Registrar must decline re-registration applications for CSPs whose previous registration was cancelled within two years due to non-compliance, serving as a "cooling-off" period.

sections.label: Penalties for non-compliance
sections.summary: Non-compliance carries fines up to $100,000 for the CSP and its senior management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Non-compliance carries significant penalties, with fines up to $100,000 for the CSP and its senior management.

sections.label: Duty to detect financial crimes
sections.summary: The Bill imposes a duty to detect or prevent money laundering, terrorism financing and proliferation financing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill imposes on them a duty to detect or prevent money laundering, terrorism financing and proliferation financing .

sections.label: Accounting or related skill exclusion
sections.summary: Clause 3(2) states services are not caught unless they require an accounting or related skill, though boundaries remain unclear.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Clause 3(2) then goes on to state that such services will not be caught by this new law "unless they require the application of an accounting or related skill." This might at first glance seem to exclude lawyers providing tax services, but the boundaries of the Bill are not so clear.

sections.label: Clarification of accounting skill term
sections.summary: The term's existing legislative context differs from the Bill, so clarification of legislative intent and meaning is sought.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The context of the term's use in the existing legislation appears to be different from that which is proposed in the Bill today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It would be helpful if the Government could clarify the legislative intent on this point and on what is meant by the term "accounting or related skill" as it is referred to in this Bill.

sections.label: Regulating taxation services for AML
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether all taxation service providers should be regulated for AML/CFT/PF purposes and why the Bill's scope is limited.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But a question that nonetheless deserves to be asked is whether persons providing "taxation services" should be regulated for AML/CFT/PF purposes regardless of whether these tax services have any connection to accounting at all.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is particularly in light of the fact that serious tax offences are, in themselves, predicate offences for AML/CFT/PF purposes and may in fact be considered to be an area of heightened risk.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I understand that some other jurisdictions, including the UK and Germany, do extend CDD obligations to providers of tax services as such.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, my third clarification is this: has the Government considered whether all persons providing taxation services should simply be regulated for AML/CFT purposes, and if so, why the scope of regulation in the proposed Bill has been limited in the way that it is?

sections.label: Law firms and CSP Bill
sections.summary: A member asks whether the Corporate Service Providers Bill will apply to practising lawyers and law firms, noting existing due diligence rules.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In any event, law firms are already required to conduct extensive due diligence checks under the Legal Profession (Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism) Rules 2015.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would be grateful if the Minister could clarify whether the Corporate Service Providers Bill will be applicable to practicing lawyers and law firms, if at all.

sections.label: Proving corporation's state of mind
sections.summary: A member asks how the requirement to prove a corporation's state of mind will be assessed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Minister clarify how the requirement to prove a corporation's "state of mind" will be assessed?

sections.label: Art market AML regulation
sections.summary: A member asks whether there are plans to include the art market in Singapore's AML/CFT/PF regulatory framework.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: FATF has identified trade in art, antiquities and other cultural objects as a market that is vulnerable to money laundering and terrorist financing risks; and so my last question is this: are there any plans to specifically include the art market within the scope of Singapore’s AML/CFT/PF regulatory framework?

sections.label: Regulating corporate service providers
sections.summary: Regulating CSPs safeguards the economy from money laundering and terrorism financing, and foreign companies must lodge returns on their registers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: By regulating CSPs, we are taking a significant step towards safeguarding our economy from the perils of money laundering, proliferation and terrorism financing, which are critical for maintaining national and international financial integrity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In a globalised era where cross-border operations are the norm, mandating that foreign companies lodge returns on their registers sends a clear message that Singapore is committed to a level playing field where every corporate entity, both local and foreign, are held to the same stringent standards.

sections.label: Lessons from money laundering cases
sections.summary: A member asks how lessons from the recent surge in money laundering cases were woven into consideration of the Bills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Moreover, given the recent surge in money laundering cases, it is also critical to understand how the lessons learnt have been woven into the considerations of these Bills.

sections.label: Impact of amendments on businesses
sections.summary: A member asks whether the Ministry assessed the administrative and financial impact of the amendments on businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Has the Ministry conducted an assessment on the administrative and financial impact of these amendments on businesses?

sections.label: Financial crime measures business impact
sections.summary: The approach to combating financial crimes must not create red tape, undermine business efficiency or deter potential investors relocating here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is critical that our approach to combat financial crimes does not inadvertently cause more detriment to us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We must ensure that while casting our net wide to catch the perpetrators, we do not entangle ourselves in red tape and undermine our business efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What are the risks that these new measures will deter potential investments by individuals seeking to relocate here?

sections.label: Maintaining controller and shareholder particulars
sections.summary: Maintaining and updating particulars of controllers, nominee directors and shareholders establishes a framework deterring illicit activities and fostering transparency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: By ensuring that the particulars of controllers, nominee directors and shareholders are meticulously maintained and regularly updated, we are establishing a robust framework that deters illicit activities and fosters a more transparent business environment.

sections.label: High regulatory standards benefits
sections.summary: High standards of regulation fortify defenses against financial crimes and enhance Singapore's attractiveness as a premier business hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: By establishing high standards of regulation, we are not only fortifying our defenses against financial crimes, but also enhancing the attractiveness of Singapore as a premier business hub.

sections.label: CSP, ACRA and CLLP Bills
sections.summary: The CSP, ACRA and CLLP Bills aim to enhance transparency, combat illicit financial activities and maintain Singapore's reputation as a trusted financial hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
sentences.text: The CSP Bill, along with the ACRA and CLLP Bills mark significant strides to solidify Singapore's regulatory landscape.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
sentences.text: These legislative measures aim to enhance transparency, combat illicit financial activities and maintain Singapore's reputation as a trusted global financial hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
sentences.text: The CSP Bill seeks to regulate entities offering corporate services, ensuring they are registered, meet the necessary criteria and operate in compliance with legal and regulatory standards.

sections.label: Penalties for non-compliance
sections.summary: Non-compliance penalties include fines, imprisonment, suspension or cancellation of registration, censuring and financial penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
sentences.text: Penalties for non-compliance include fines, imprisonment, suspension or cancellation of registration and regulatory actions, such as censuring and financial penalties.

sections.label: Stricter regulations fewer service providers
sections.summary: Stricter regulations might result in fewer service providers meeting the new criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
sentences.text: Lastly, stricter regulations might also result in fewer service providers meeting the new criteria.

sections.label: CSP duties on nominee directors
sections.summary: Section 16 imposes duties on CSPs to ensure nominee directors are fit and proper, requiring reasonable steps and prescribed factors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Section 16 will impose duties on CSPs to ensure that a nominee director is a fit and proper person.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Section 16(2) requires a CSP to take all reasonable steps to be satisfied that the person is not disqualified from acting as a director and to consider prescribed factors.

sections.label: Financial penalties for contraventions
sections.summary: Sections 19(2)(d) and 21(2)(d) allow financial penalties of $25,000 and $10,000 per contravention, with additional daily fines for continuing offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under sections 19(2)(d) and 21(2)(d), financial penalties of $25,000 and $10,000 respectively may be imposed for each contravention or non-compliance of regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For certain continuing offences, the Bill prescribes additional fines to be imposed for every day during which the offence continues after conviction.

sections.label: Money laundering case examples
sections.summary: The $3 billion money laundering case and a US$1 million scam proceeds case are examples of money launderers exploiting Singapore's financial system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The $3 billion money laundering case last year and more recently, a case of US$1 million in scam proceeds channeled through two companies incorporated here, are two examples of money launderers trying to take advantage of our financial system.

sections.label: Expanded CSP registration requirements
sections.summary: Clause 7 expands registration requirements for CSPs even if they do not file transactions for clients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Clause 7 expands the registration requirements for CSPs, even if they do not file transactions on behalf of their clients.

sections.label: Criminal liability for AML breaches
sections.summary: Clauses 16, 17, 29 and 30 impose criminal liability on registered CSPs and senior management for AML/CFT/PF breaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Clauses 16, 17, 29 and 30 imposes criminal liability on registered CSPs and their senior management for breaches of AML/CFT/PF requirements.

sections.label: Questions on fit and proper criteria
sections.summary: The speaker asks what criteria determine a nominee director's fitness and how CSPs verify it without comprehensive background data, seeking clear definition and workshops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Regarding clauses 16 and 37 for the new requirements for nominee directors, I would like to ask, what criteria will be used to determine if an individual is "fit and proper" to act as a nominee director and how will CSPs verify this information without access to comprehensive background data? "Fit and proper" must be clearly defined and the nominee director should be required to attend workshops relating to director's duties and responsibilities.

sections.label: Members reference money laundering case
sections.summary: Members made reference to the $3 billion money laundering case in their speeches.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In their speeches, Members made reference to the $3 billion money laundering case.

sections.label: CSP registration and RQI requirements
sections.summary: CSPs must be registered with ACRA and appoint a Registered Qualified Individual meeting qualification requirements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In summary, CSPs are required to be a registered business entity with ACRA and must appoint a Registered Qualified Individual (RQI) who meets the qualification requirements.

sections.label: Accounting providers designated activity registration
sections.summary: Only accounting service providers carrying out FATF-designated money laundering risk activities need to register as a CSP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Amongst accounting service providers, only those that carry out any designated activity defined by FATF to have money laundering risks, need to register as a CSP.

sections.label: Two-year reapplication ban after cancellation
sections.summary: After a cancellation, entities and individuals cannot reapply for registration for two years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Following a cancellation, entities and individuals are not allowed to reapply for registration for a period of two years.

sections.label: Fit and proper factors for directors
sections.summary: Fit and proper factors will be prescribed in subsidiary legislation, including conduct, compliance history, integrity, competency, capacity and capability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The "fit and proper" factors will be prescribed in subsidiary legislation, but would include assessing an individual's conduct and compliance history, integrity and whether the person has the competency, capacity and capability to fulfil his obligations as a director.

sections.label: Proposal dropped after public consultation
sections.summary: It was included in inter-agency discussions and public consultation, but after feedback the proposal was not proceeded with.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: It is included in the inter-agency discussions and conducting of public consultation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But after considering the feedback received, we decided not to go ahead with that proposal.

sections.label: Maximum fine quantum consistency
sections.summary: The maximum fine of up to $100,000 for such breaches is consistent with other designated non-financial businesses and professions in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The quantum of up to $100,000 for the maximum fine of such breaches is also consistent with those of other designated non-financial businesses and professions in Singapore.

sections.label: Appeals to Minister
sections.summary: Clause 23 of the Bill allows appeals to the Minister for regulatory actions if further actions are taken.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: If further actions are taken, clause 23 of the Bill allows for appeals to the Minister for regulatory actions.

sections.label: Fines for inaccurate registers
sections.summary: Companies that do not maintain accurate and up to date information in their registers can face fines, which the Bill enhances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Companies that do not maintain accurate and up to date information in their registers can face fines, which we are enhancing as part of this Bill.

sections.label: Compliance costs and business ease
sections.summary: The new requirements in the Bills are not expected to significantly increase compliance costs on CSPs or affect ease of doing business in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: On the whole, we do not expect the new requirements in the Bills to significantly increase compliance costs on CSPs or affect the ease of doing business in Singapore.

sections.label: CSP registration and transition
sections.summary: All CSPs must register as CSPs; existing Registered Filing Agents transit seamlessly without re-registering until expiry, and unregistered entities have six months after commencement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For the requirement for all CSPs to register as CSPs, even if they do not transact with ACRA, existing Registered Filing Agents will be transited seamlessly and need not re-register with ACRA, until their existing registration expires.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Entities that have not yet registered with ACRA will have six months to do so after the commencement of the new CSP regime.

sections.label: Mandatory AML/CFT courses
sections.summary: CSPs must complete mandatory AML/CFT courses for registration and renewal, currently a half-day course with a one-hour test and 80% pass mark.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The CSPs must complete mandatory AML/CFT courses, as part of the registration and renewal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: My understanding on the intensity of the course and this is not set in stone because, obviously, this may be adjusted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But at the moment, it is a half-day course by professional instructors with about a one-hour test, subsequently; and the pass mark is 80%.

sections.label: Combating financial crime amendments
sections.summary: The Government states these amendments strengthen the regulatory regime for CSPs and minimise misuse of legal persons to combat financial crime.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Government has always taken our responsibilities to combat financial crime seriously, even before the authorities uncovered the $3 billion money laundering case last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, I am grateful for the support and for our unity, as a society, in recognising the need for and the importance of combating financial crime.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: These amendments will further advance our efforts to combat financial crime, by strengthening our regulatory regime for CSPs and minimising the misuse of legal persons.

sections.label: Defining key appointment holder
sections.summary: The speaker says defining the term precisely is difficult, but the definitive word in key appointment holder is key.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: On the second point, I think it is very difficult to define really precisely, but when you have a term like key appointment holder, the definitive word is "key".

sections.label: Training courses for directorships
sections.summary: The speaker restates Mr Chua's question about whether training courses can be required when a person exceeds a certain number of directorships.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: On the first question, if I understood Mr Chua correctly, he was saying, "Can we still not have training courses when a person exceeds a certain number of directorships".

sections.label: Nominee director obligations and competence
sections.summary: Nominee directors have the same obligations as other directors, and individuals, appointers and companies should determine fitness and competence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: A nominee director has the same obligations as any other directors – you have fiduciary duties and this is certain minimal level of competence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We decided that it would be better for the individuals and the persons appointing them and the companies to determine whether this person is fit and proper and has the right competence.

sections.label: No art market regulatory regime
sections.summary: The speaker says there is no intention at the moment to create a legislative regime for the art market.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: All I can say is that I have not been looking at that, at this stage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, I could not rule it out sometime in the future, but as far as I am aware, and I am not speaking for any other Ministries, but in the course of looking at the work, we were not looking for a regulatory regime for the art market.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: That said, it does not mean that art would be excluded from examination in the context of looking at anti-money laundering.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Anything which is an asset and has value can potentially be a receptacle for illicit funds to be parked in and then later on, transacted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I think the best way I can summarise it, is that there is no, at the moment, an intention to do a legislative regime for this.
